Complete these steps **in order** before the workshop:

::: {.setup-path}
<span><strong>1</strong> R</span>
<span class="path-arrow">→</span>
<span><strong>2</strong> RStudio</span>
<span class="path-arrow">→</span>
<span><strong>3</strong> Packages</span>
:::

## 1. Install R

R is the statistical computing engine that runs your code.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Windows

1. Go to [CRAN for Windows](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/).
2. Download the current **R for Windows** installer (`.exe`).
3. Run the installer and follow the prompts. The default options are suitable for this workshop.

### macOS

1. Go to [CRAN for macOS](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/).
2. Download the current installer (`.pkg`) that matches your Mac.
3. Open the downloaded file and follow the prompts.
4. Install [XQuartz](https://www.xquartz.org/) only if R or a package later reports that it is required.

### Linux

1. Open the [CRAN Linux instructions](https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux).
2. Select your distribution and follow its current installation instructions.
3. On Debian or Ubuntu, the basic installation normally uses:

   ```bash
   sudo apt update
   sudo apt install r-base
   ```

4. On Fedora, follow CRAN's Fedora instructions or install R through your system's package manager.
:::

## 2. Install RStudio Desktop

RStudio is the editor used during the workshop. It provides the Console, script editor, Environment, plots, files, and help in one place.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Windows

1. Open the [RStudio Desktop download page](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/#download).
2. Under **Installers**, select the Windows version.
3. Run the downloaded installer.
4. Open RStudio. If it starts without an error, RStudio has found your R installation.

### macOS

1. Open the [RStudio Desktop download page](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/#download).
2. Under **Installers**, select the macOS version.
3. Open the downloaded `.dmg` and drag RStudio to **Applications**.
4. Open RStudio. If it starts without an error, RStudio has found your R installation.

### Linux

1. Open the [RStudio Desktop download page](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/#download).
2. Select the installer matching your Linux distribution, such as the `.deb` installer for Ubuntu.
3. Install the downloaded package using your distribution's normal software installer.
4. Open RStudio to confirm that it starts correctly.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
Already have R and RStudio? Open RStudio and use **Help → Check for Updates**. A recent version is recommended.
:::

## 3. Install the packages

Open RStudio and click inside the **Console** panel. Copy the following command, paste it after the `>` prompt, and press **Enter**:

```r
install.packages(c("readxl", "tidyverse"))
```

Installation may take several minutes. Messages and warnings are common; an `ERROR` message means that something needs attention.

When installation finishes, you can test if the packages can be loaded:

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
```

If a there are no error messages, the software is ready. Warnings are normal.

## Troubleshooting

### RStudio cannot find R

Close RStudio, reinstall R, and then open RStudio again. Remember that R must be installed first.

### A package did not install

Restart RStudio and run the installation command again. Copy the complete final error message if you need to ask for help.

### Still stuck?

Report installation problems before the workshop by emailing [jan.gacnik@ijs.si](mailto:jan.gacnik@ijs.si). Include your operating system and a screenshot or copy of the complete error message.

::: {.setup-complete}
### Setup complete

You are ready when RStudio opens and both packages load without errors.
